IS : 1333 - 1978

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR INK, DUPLICATING, FOR SINGLE DRUM ROTARY MACHINE

( Second Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 July 1978, after the draft finalized by the Inks and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was originally issued in 1958 and subsequently revised in 1973. In the first revision additional requirements for fineness of dispersion, fluidity and freedom from smudginess were added and changes were made in the procedure for evaluating performance, stability, strike-through and offset. In the present revision, relative density has been specified instead of the requirement of fluidity. The requirement of oil halation has been dropped. Changes have also been made in the method of evaluating performance of the material and in the requirement of fineness of dispersion. 0.3 This standard contains clauses 3.2 and 5.1 which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for duplicating ink, all weather, for single drum rotarv machines.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 3

IS : 1333 - 1978

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 47241968* shall apply. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description -- The material shall be either oil based or emulsion based. It shall flow satisfactorily through ink pad and screen. It shall be free from grit and other objectionable matter capable of clogging the ink pad and screen. It shall not possess any objectionable odour. 3.2 Colour -- The colour shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 3.3 Stability -- The material shall be workable in all types of weather and shall satisfy the test prescribed in 7.2. 3.4 Fineness of Dispersion -- When tested for fineness of dispersion of pigment particles in the medium by the method prescribed in Appendix A, the material shall not be coarser than 15 microns on the Hegman gauge or equivalent. 3.5 Relative Density -- When tested in accordance with the method prescribed in Appendix B, the relative density of the material shall be not greater than 1.05 nor less than 0.97 at 27 � 1�C. 3.6 Performance -- The performance of the material shall be such that it passes the test prescribed in C-4.1 and C-4.3. 3.7 Strike-Through and Offset -- The ink shall not show any strikethrough or offset when examined as described in C-4.2. 3.8 Smudginess -- The impressions obtained with the ink shall not smudge after drying when tested by the method prescribed in Appendix D. 4. KEEPING QUALITY 4.1 The material shall be in Workable condition for at least two years from the date of manufacture when stored under normal conditions. 5. PACKING AND MARKING 5.1 Packing -- The material shall be packed in suitable containers, the net mass in each being 400 g, or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
*Glossary of terms relating to printing inkes and allied industries.

4

IS : 1333 - 1978

5.2 Marking -- The containers shall be securely closed and marked with the following information: a) Name and colour of the material; b) Name of the manufacturer and/or his recognized trade-mark, if any; c) Net mass of the material; d) Identification in code or otherwise to enable the date and lot of manufacture to be traced back from records; and e) Brief instructions for use. 5.2.1 The containers may also be marked with the Standard Mark. NOTE -- The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6. SAMPLING 6.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn and adjudged as prescribed in Appendix E. 7. TEST METHODS 7.1 Tests for the requirements laid down in 3.3 to 3.8 shall be carried out as prescribed in 7.2, and Appendices A, B, C and D. 7.2 Test for Stability 7.2.1 Take about 10 g of the material in a porcelain crucible ( see designation 1/60 of IS : 2837 ( Part I )-1975* with a well fitted lid and keep it at a temperature of 0�C for 3 hours. Keep it in a similar manner at a temperature of 60 � 2�C for 3 hours. The material shall not show any sign of appreciable variation in consistency or any separation of vehicle or any sign of bubbles when observed after allowing it to attain room temperature. 7.2.2 Take 100 ml of the material in a glass cylinder with a well fitted stopper of 250-ml capacity. Allow to keep for 15 days at ambient temperature. The ink shall be considered to have passed the test if there is no separation of the vehicle.
*Specification for porcelain crucibles and basins: Part I Crucibles ( first revision ).

IS : 1333 - 1978

APPENDIX A ( Clauses 3.4 and 7.1 )
DETERMINATION OF FINENESS OF DISPERSION A-0. GENERAL A-0.1 Fineness of dispersion is measured on a grind gauge. It consists of a block of hardened steel into which has been machined a shallow groove varying in depth from zero at one end to 0.102 mm at the other. A sample of ink is placed at the 'deep' end and is drawn down towards the shallow end by a steel scraper. Observation of any scratches in the ink film, and where they occur in terms of distance along the gauge, gives a measure of the degree of dispersion in the ink sample. A-1. APPARATUS A-1.1 Gauge* -- a hardened steel block approximately 180 mm in length, 60 to 65 mm in width and 10 to 15 mm in thickness. The top surface of the block shall be ground smooth and flat, and shall contain a groove 133 mm in length and 12.5 mm in width, centred in the top of the block. The groove shall be tapered uniformly in depth length-wise from 0.102 mm at one end to zero depth at the other, calibrated with a scale number in accordance with its depth as given in Table 1.
NOTE -- The apparatus may also be of a double channel type for comparing another sample.

A-1.1.1 Care of Gauge -- The gauge shall be immediately cleaned after each reading. Use a solvent and soft cloth. Keep the gauge covered at all times when not in use. Gauges that lie idle for extended periods of time shall be protected from rust. Do not allow any hard materials to come in contact with the gauge surface or scraper in any manner that might result in scarring or nicking. Tapping or scratching with other metallic surfaces shall be avoided. A-1.2 Scraper -- a double edged steel blade 87.5 mm long, 37.5 mm wide and 6.8 mm thick. The two edges along the length shall be, rounded to a radius of approximately 0.25 mm. A-1.2.1 The scraper edge is rendered unsatisfactory for use by wear of the contact edge or by warpage. Wear or warpage of the scraper can be observed by facing the edge of the scraper down on the smooth level face of the gauge and then inspecting the contact edge by means of a strong light, placed behind the gauge. Rocking the scraper forward or backward will reveal poor contact due to wear or warpage. If any face shows that the scraper has been damaged, it shall not be used.
*Generally known as Hegman gauge.

6

IS : 1333 - 1978
TABLE 1 RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DEPTH OF TAPERED GROOVE AND SCALE FOR FINENESS OF GRINDING ( Clause A-1.1 )
DISTANCE FROM ZERO END DEPTH HEGMAN SCALE

(1) mm 133 127 111 95 79 63 48 32 16 0

(2) microns 102 102 89 76 64 51 38 25 13 0

(3) Well for sample 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8

A-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Place the gauge on a flat, non-slippery surface, and wipe it clean immediately before the test. Put the material to be tested in the deep end of the groove of the gauge so that it overflows the groove slightly. Care shall be taken to see that the material is free of air bubbles. Using both hands, hold the blade perpendicular to the block surface and at right angles to the length of the groove, draw the material down the length of the groove wtth a uniform deliberate motion. Use sufficient pressure to clean the level face of the gauge. Immediately read the fineness as follows: a) View the gauge from the side so that the line of vision is at right angles to the longer dimension of the groove; b) Hold the gauge in light that will make the pattern readily visible; c) For actual reading, make the angle between the face of the gauge and the line of vision not more than 30� nor less than 20�; and d) Interpret the pattern and designate dispersion in microns or scale number, ignoring the few isolated and irregularly spaced particles towards the deep end of the groove. A-2.1.1 Using a fresh sample of the material each time, obtain three readings in like manner. The first draw down and reading is preliminary in order to establish proper conditions and to locate the fineness pattern.
7

IS : 1333 - 1978 With this known, the second and third readings can be made with a minimum time lapse between completion of draw and actual reading. No reading shall be considered for reporting fineness when the time lapse exceeds 10 seconds.

APPENDIX B ( Clauses 3.5 and 7.1 )
DETERMINATION OF RELATIVE DENSITY B-11. APPARATUS B-1.1 Pyknometer ( Hubbard Type ) -- See Type 6 of IS : 57171970*. B-2. PROCEDURE B-2.1 Clean, dry and weigh the bottle with stopper. Fill with water at a temperature of about 25�C, introduce the stopper and keep it in a water bath at 27 � 1�C for 15 minutes. Wipe off all surplus water from the surface with a soft, clean and dry cloth and weigh again. Empty the bottle, clean and dry it, and repeat the operations after filling it with the material. B-3. CALCULATION B-3.1 Relative density = where M2 = mass in g of pyknometer with stopper filled with the material, M = mass in g of the dry pyknometer with stopper, and M1 = mass in g of the pyknometer filled with distilled water.
*Specification for pyknometers.

APPENDIX C ( Clauses 3.6, 3.7 and 7.1 )
TEST POR PERFORMANCE, STRIKE-THROUGH AND OFFSET C-1. DUPLICATING MACHINE C-1.1 An electrically operated single-sealed drum, internally inked, rotary duplicating machine capable of taking up paper of maximum width 230 mm, shall be used. The machine shall work at touch pressure so as to produce continuous impression of uniform depth throughout the area under print. Rubber impression roller shall have Shore hardness between 30 and 35. C-2. STENCIL PAPER C-2.1 The stencil paper shall conform to IS : 5086-1969*. C-3. DUPLICATING PAPER C-3.1 White duplicating, semi-absorbent paper [ see Sl No. (X) of Table 1 of IS : 1848-1971 ] having a substance of 75 g/m2 with a tolerance of � 2.5 percent, shall be used. C-4. PROCEDURE C-4.1 Test for Performance C-4.1.1 Clean the drum of the machine internally, the impression roller, ink screen and the pad with due care. Cut the stencil with 25 lines of typed matter, each 15 cm long using all the letters, capitals and lower case, along with numerals and symbols. Set the machine at the speed of 125 � 5 sheets per minute. C-4.1.2 Performance Test at 45 � 2�C -- Heat approximately 300 g of ink to 45 � 2�C and pour it in the drum previously emptied ( pouring time shall not exceed 3 minutes ) and run the machine till the ink spreads evenly on the ink pad. Take out 250 sheets with both sides printing ( total 500 copies ). C-4.1.3 Performance Test at 10 � 2�C -- Store about 300 g of ink at 10 � 2�C for 3 hours, pour the ink in the drum previously emptied ( pouring time shall not exceed 3 minutes ) and run the machine till the ink spreads evenly on the ink pad. Take out 250 sheets with both sides printing ( total 500 copies ).
*Specification for stencil paper. Specification for writing and printing papers ( first revison ).

9

IS : 1333 - 1978 C-4.1.4 The ink shall be considered to have satisfied the requirements of the test if all the sheets duplicated at C-4.1.2 and C-4.1.3, except first 20 sheets in each case, are clear and legible without blurring of characters. C-4.2 Test for Strike-Through and Offset -- Examine all the sheets duplicated at 45 � 2�C and 10 � 2�C respectively except first 20 sheets. The ink shall not show any strike-through and offset sufficient to interfere with the ligibility of the finished work on either side of the paper. When the printed copies are stacked, there shall be no objectionable transfer of ink from one sheet to the other. C-4.3 Store away the stencil used for performance test in C-4.1 at two different temperatures, namely, 45 � 2�C and 10 � 2�C in between two sheets of blotting paper. Before storing, blot out excess of ink from the stencil sheet. .After 15 days, use this stencil again and repeat the performance test at two temperatures at laid down under C-4.1.2 and C-4.1.3. Observe 250 copies printed on both sides at 45 � 2�C and 10 � 2�C. The printing shall be uniform without any sign of breaking of letters out on the stencil.

A P P E N D I X D ( Clauses 3.8 and 7.1 ) TEST FOR SMUDGINESS D-1. PROCEDURE D-1.1 Take a printed sheet as taken out in C-4.1 which has been allowed to dry for two minutes and place it on a smooth flat surface with the printed side up and cover with a clean sheet of a duplicating paper. Place a 100-g weight of 24 mm diameter ( see IS : 1056-1965* ) on one edge of the paper and draw the clean sheet of duplicating paper and the weight slowly across the printed sheet. Repeat this test twice and examine after each test. The material shall be considered to have passed the test if there is no smudging or spreading of the ink on the printed sheet.
*Specification for commercial weights ( revised ).

IS : 1333 - 1978 APPENDIX ( Clause 6.1 ) E

SAMPLING OF INK, DUPLICATING, FOR SINGLE DRUM ROTARY MACHINE E-1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR SAMPLING E-1.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling test samples, the following precautions and directions shall be observed. E-1.1 Samples shall be drawn from original unopened containers. E-1.2 Samples shall not be taken in an exposed place. E-1.3 Each sample container shall be marked with full details of sampling and the month and year of manufacture of the material. E-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING E-2.1 All the containers in a single consignment of the material drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared or known to consist of different batches of manufacture, the containers belonging to the same batch shall be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. E-2.1.1 Samples of duplicating ink shall be tested from each lot for ascertaining the conformity of the material to the requirements of the specification. B-2.2 The number of containers to be chosen from the lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 2.
TABLE 2 NUMBER OF CONTAINERS TO BE SELECTED FOR SAMPLING
LOT SIZE
(N)

NO. OF CONTAINERS TO BE

CHOSEN
(n)

(1)

Up to 200 201 and above

(2) 6 9

11

IS : 1333 - 1978 E-2.3 These containers shall be chosen at random from the lot. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, random number tables shall be used ( see IS : 4905-1968* ). In the absence of random number tables, the following procedure may be adopted: Starting from any container in the lot, count them as 1, 2, 3,..., up to r and so on. Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn from the lot to give the required sample size, r being the integral part of N/n, where N is the lot size and n is the sample size. E-3. PREPARATION OF TEST SAMPLES E-3.1 Divide the selected containers into three equal sets. Each set shall be labelled with full details of sampling. One set shall be sent to the purchaser and one to the supplier. E-3.2 Referee Set -- The third set, bearing the seals of the purchaser and the supplier shall constitute the referee set and shall be used in case of dispute between the two. It shall be kept at a place agreed to between them. E-3.3 The material of all the containers in a set shall be transferred to a suitable sample container and stirred to yield a homogeneous test sample. E-4. NUMBER OF TESTS E-4.1 All the characteristics given in the specification shall be tested on the test sample prepared as prescribed in E-3. E-5. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY E-5.1 The lot shall be declared to have complied with the requirements of the specification if all the tests in respect of different characteristics give satisfactory results.

*Methods of random sampling.
